general.temas: The most frequently covered issue is Lula’s decree regulating the end of the 6×1 work schedule. Other topics include the meeting of Trump, Xi and Putin, fiscal adjustment, the composition of the future cabinet and issues related to January 8. Only Folha de S.Paulo highlights the International Court of Justice’s ruling against Myanmar for genocide against the Rohingya.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are moderate: coverage mentions the dispute in the Supreme Court over working hours, unease among its justices over police reports and divisions within the PL over leadership of Congress. Investigations linked to January 8 and an allegation of racism in São Paulo also appear. Internationally, the ruling on the genocide of the Rohingya reflects a grave conflict. News about sport, culture, science and health partly balances this picture.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- The International Court of Justice concludes that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.
- Brazil’s beef supply falls and prices rise.
- The government’s fiscal adjustment could advance in the Chamber of Deputies without substantial changes; Lula criticizes speculation about his cabinet.
- Police are investigating an allegation of racism made by actress Adriana Lessa at a luxury shopping mall.
- The front page includes news about technology, science, health and culture, including the purchase of an AI supercomputer.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: The language is mostly straightforward and informative, although expressions such as “next major blackout” and “destroying the image” add a somewhat sensationalist tone.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines political, economic and social issues with technology, health and entertainment. There is no clear political bias in the headlines.

O Globo.resumen:
- The decree on the 5x2 work schedule changes how working hours and overtime are calculated.
- The Central Bank announces a dollar auction; the FGC questions the failure to disclose BRB’s balance sheet.
- Two analyses address the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin.
- The front page includes news about a colonel under investigation in connection with January 8 and a request to visit Bolsonaro.
- Other prominent stories include fears of a Super El Niño in Peru, New Year’s programming in Rio, and business and football news.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The tone is mostly informative, although expressions such as “Super El Niño threat,” “hostage” and “usurp power” add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
O Globo.sesgo: The selection prioritizes the economic consequences of public decisions and scrutiny of authorities and institutions. Its international politics coverage includes analyses with explicit interpretations, but no conclusive overall ideological orientation is apparent.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Lula defends fiscal restraint, signs a decree on the 6x1 work schedule and promises to create a Ministry for Older People.
- Natália Resende declines to comment on Tarcísio’s succession.
- The dollar reaches R$ 5.92 and Wall Street indexes rise, led by technology stocks.
- São Paulo’s city government plans a free international show; a bookshop celebrates its anniversary and a Van Gogh painting sets an auction record.
- The front page includes news about GTA 6 and presents Flamengo as close to winning the Brasileirão title.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is mostly informative, although expressions such as “the dollar soars” and “with hands and feet on the trophy” add emphasis and a certain sense of spectacle.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines politics and economics with culture, video games and sport. There is no clear political bias in the headlines.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- A column questions the STF’s immunity criteria; other reports point to tensions within the court.
- Lula’s government regulates the 5×2 work schedule and the Chamber of Deputies approves fines for obstructing the presidential transition.
- The PL is divided over the leadership of the Chamber of Deputies.
- A Trump official reportedly suggested that Guyana cede part of Essequibo to Venezuela; the meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi is also analyzed.
- The front page covers an alleged diesel scheme, a health alert, cooperatives, cinema and remarks by the pope.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: The phrase “immunity for friends” suggests favoritism and oversimplifies how the STF works, while “ghost ship” adds drama; most of the other headlines are informative.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The selection highlights institutional and political conflicts, with one headline taking a critical approach to the STF. The rest combines international, economic and social issues with straightforward news coverage.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- Lula signs a decree on the transition from the 6×1 to the 5×2 work schedule; the fiscal debate and a possible cabinet reshuffle are also covered.
- The UN warns about the concentration of power in AI; Trump, Xi and Putin propose reforming the organization and holding talks on nuclear weapons.
- A COP31 draft removes the reference to moving away from fossil fuels; Brasília hosts a forum on environmental education and climate.
- The deadline to request a resit of the Enem expires, while Moraes awaits a response from prosecutors before deciding on house arrest for a person convicted in connection with January 8.
- A poll shows a close race in Argentina; Corinthians moves out of the relegation zone and the front page includes the day’s tarot reading.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: The tone is mostly informative, although expressions such as “medieval model,” “disappears” and “musical chairs” add drama; there is no explicit opposition between the people and the elites.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The selection gives extensive space to public policy, climate and international affairs. The question of what kind of country people want to finance introduces a value-laden perspective into the fiscal debate.

opiniones.comunista:
I welcome the decree regulating the end of the 6×1 schedule: working people have a right to time to rest and live, without losing pay or rights. But I know that a legal victory requires vigilance and collective organization to become a reality. At the same time, I am concerned that the fiscal adjustment is advancing rapidly: the question is not just how much the state spends, but who pays and which needs go unmet. I will not accept budget discipline being used as an excuse to weaken public services.

The concentration of power over artificial intelligence and the debate over Enel’s concession raise a common question: why leave essential infrastructure subject to the logic of profit? I advocate collective ownership and democratic control of energy and technology, so that their benefits meet the needs of the majority rather than those of big capital.
opiniones.anarquista:
I welcome the end of the 6×1 schedule: having more time of one’s own is a gain for freedom, not a favor from those in power. But I do not want the debate to end with a decree. As long as other people decide how we work and what we do with what we produce, our time will remain subject to someone else’s authority. I prefer independent unions, assemblies and workplaces managed by those who keep them running.

The UN’s warning about the concentration of power in artificial intelligence points to another problem: a handful of entities can impose tools and standards that affect millions. Changing the people at the top is not enough for me. I advocate transparent, accessible technologies under collective control, alongside mutual aid networks that allow us to depend less on both governments and big companies.
opiniones.liberal:
I welcome the progress of the fiscal adjustment, but passing it is not enough: I want a limited state that spends less and makes it possible to lower taxes sustainably. Every real that remains in the hands of the person who earns it is an opportunity to save, invest or support a family. Fiscal responsibility is not a whim of the market; it protects everyone’s freedom from debt that taxpayers will have to pay.

I also want workers to have more rest. But imposing a uniform work schedule can raise costs and make hiring more difficult, especially for small businesses. I prefer voluntary agreements that take into account the needs of each activity and a more productive economy capable of offering better wages without excluding those looking for work. Freedom requires the ability to choose, but also taking responsibility for our decisions.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
Today I see a Brazil that needs to regain control of its destiny. I am concerned that the purchase of an artificial intelligence supercomputer depends on Washington’s approval: a sovereign nation cannot entrust its technological future to authorization from another power. We need to develop our own capabilities, even if that requires patience and clear priorities.

I also distrust a fiscal adjustment that could pass through the Chamber of Deputies without substantial changes or sufficient public debate. Responsibility for the public finances must not serve as an excuse to protect the privileged while families face rising meat prices. And on the new work schedule, I want more time for family, but not promises that end up hurting small business owners and employment. Brazil needs production, discipline and governments that answer to their people, not to political elites or foreign interests.
opiniones.centro:
I welcome Brazil’s move toward a work schedule with two days off. Free time is also a matter of dignity. But lasting labor reform needs a gradual transition, dialogue with workers and businesses, and attention to its effects on employment. Protecting rights and preserving the ability to hire are not opposing goals.

I also support fiscal adjustment, provided there is a transparent discussion of which spending is prioritized and whom the decisions affect. Sound public finances support both economic confidence and social services; they are not an end in themselves. That is why I am concerned about the refusal to disclose documents on BRB’s financial position: the public has a right to know what is at stake. And the International Court of Justice’s decision on the Rohingya is a reminder that international institutions matter when they must respond to atrocities.
